A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Skywork-Reward-V2, SynPref-40M, and the same two-stage curation pipeline. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial appendix expansion and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original reward-model evaluations, best-of-N experiments, and data-curation and annotation ablations in Sections 4.2-4.4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains those results and adds original downstream policy evaluations, human-agreement studies, privacy tests, and filtering and annotation experiments in Appendices D, E, and H.

M1.justification: The Bradley-Terry objective, adaptive retrieval rule with k_max = 8, human-guided LLM labeling, dual-reward-model filtering, and flipped-label recycling remain. Section 3 expands the explanation of the two retrieval operations and filtering decisions; the unchanged Figure 3 supports treating these as clarifications rather than a new algorithm.

E1.justification: The seven original reward-model benchmarks remain, while Appendix H.2 adds downstream policy optimization and evaluation on ArenaHard v1/v2, MT-Bench, and WildBench. Appendix D.3 adds test scenarios with personal information removed or replaced. Newly disclosed language and task distributions describe the existing mixture rather than establish changed training coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds an aggregated LLM-judge comparator, an LLM-plus-reward-model baseline without human guidance, alternative filtering combinations, and base/SFT/official-instruct policy controls in Tables 17 and 19-21. GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet also gain reported participation in PPE Correctness and RM-Bench comparisons previously left blank.

E3.justification: New protocols include policy training on selected hard prompts with two policy backbones, a 500-item human audit of preference attributes, and additional Gemma and Qwen2.5 backbone experiments. Table 3 also changes its metric description from best-of-N accuracy to pairwise accuracy on the best-of-N split, although surrounding prose remains inconsistent. This does not establish that the retained experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's retained data and first-iteration annotation ablations, v3 adds an eight-iteration control without human guidance, human verification of kept/flipped labels, broader decontamination checks, PII perturbation tests, attribute-quality audits, and backbone-generalization analysis. These directly examine annotation quality, filtering reliability, and robustness in Appendices D, E, and H.

E5.justification: Both versions primarily report point estimates and retain the single-run training curve. v3 adds no experimental seed counts, repeated-training-run summaries, confidence intervals, or significance tests. New agreement percentages and self-consistency ensemble sampling do not constitute uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive outcomes, including downstream policy results, 86%/92% human agreement for kept/flipped pairs in Table 19, and an ensemble average of 86.0 versus 88.6 for the final reward model in Table 21. Retained values also change: Table 1 revises Skywork-Reward-Llama-3.1-8B-v0.2's RM-Bench score from 72.1 to 64.7, matching v1 Figure 5 rather than establishing a performance decline.

T1.justification: Appendix F.2 adds an approximate mathematical cost model summing human-labeling, silver-labeling, and Stage 2 curation costs, together with budget-allocation constraints. This is a limited addition; the Bradley-Terry and adaptive-retrieval equations remain unchanged, and no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The principal dataset, curation-pipeline, eight-model release, and seven-benchmark leadership claims remain. v3 adds an explicit abstract-level claim of strong downstream performance. Its abstract's generative-reward-model comparison largely promotes a claim already present in v1 Section 4.2.

C2.justification: Section 2 replaces broad over-optimization interpretations with qualified statements about inconsistent cross-benchmark gains and limits the loss-modification critique to Gemma-2-27B variants. New appendices interpret intransitive preferences, filtering bias, privacy sensitivity, and differences between reward models and LLM ensembles. The original limitations are largely retained, moving from Appendix A to B.

D1.justification: v3 substantially expands documentation of data allocation, composition and licensing, retrieval operations, annotator-model lists, and human annotation staffing, costs, and duration. It also adds budgeting guidance and a repository link. Core training hyperparameters and hardware remain, while complete annotation prompts are still deferred to supplementary material outside the supplied PDFs.

R1.justification: The original related-work discussion is largely preserved in Appendix A. v3 adds references and connections concerning intransitive preferences, preference underspecification, mechanism design, and the new downstream/backbone experiments, while removing some earlier citations. Publication and bibliography corrections alone are not substantive positioning changes.

P1.justification: v3 moves related work from the main text to Appendix A, shortens the conclusion and removes the future-outlook passage, adds Section 4.5, and substantially reorganizes the appendices. It also rewrites the benchmark critique and expands method and ablation explanations, producing a substantial narrative revision beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: Main results are repacked into side-by-side displays, including v1 Figures 5 and 6 reformatted as v3 Tables 4 and 5. Numerous new appendix tables present dataset audits, annotation assessments, downstream results, and controls. The original pipeline diagram and plots are retained; their relocation or renumbering is not new scientific evidence.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens v1's predominantly offline evaluation with downstream policy results, human checks of filtering decisions, and a multi-iteration control isolating human guidance. Expanded implementation documentation also addresses important reproducibility gaps. These gains outweigh remaining weaknesses: several new studies omit sample sizes and uncertainty, some scores disagree across tables, and Appendix F.3's worked budget allocates funds inconsistently. The improvement comes from stronger practical validation and auditability, rather than increased length or higher headline scores.
